svg.aria-label: The hand-off lifecycle across two chats. As Chat A works, the stop hook saves its recap as a note on disk. When Chat B opens in the same folder, session-start shows that note as data; you say carry on, B runs the takeover command to write a takeover mark, and Chat A is then told by the prompt and pretool hooks to stop. Chat B continues as the live chat, and when it claims 100 percent the complete-check hook asks git whether the named docs really changed.
svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Inter, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: The hand-off · two chats, one piece of work
A note is written while Chat A works, shown to Chat B when it opens; the moment B takes over, A is told to stop — nothing lost, nothing run twice.
STAGE 2 — A GROWS BIG, B OPENS

g.text: Each reply ends with a recap.
mode stop saves it as A's note.

current task ends, start a new chat —
+ additionalContext: end replies with the recap

svg.text: A keeps working — or idles — until B takes over

while this file exists, A is

Codex: a history reopen keeps the mark.
When a recap says 10/10, 100%, the Stop hook asks git:
did the .md / .mdx / .txt files named in "planning docs updated"
really change — in the commits the recap lists, or the tree?
Plus a "memory updated" step on Claude Code and Grok.
Codex needs the docs step only when git shows changes
{ decision: "block", reason: "...names X, but git shows no change" }
→ otherwise the 100% reply is accepted; else blocked until fixed.
one note per chat · the mark stops the old chat · git guards the 100% claim
